notes.description: The headnote, printed above the ingredients the way a cookbook prints it — where the dish comes from, when to make it, what can be substituted, the one tip that decides whether it works. Two to four sentences of prose, not a summary of the steps. Write it last, once the whole recipe is on the page. Omit it only when there is genuinely nothing to say.

image_query.description: Two to four words for what the finished dish LOOKS like, written the way you would type it into a stock photo search box — the food, its form, and at most one visible quality: "rustic focaccia bread", "creamy mushroom pasta", "chocolate layer cake slice". Not the recipe's title, not a cuisine, not a person's or brand's name, nothing about taste, difficulty or occasion, nothing a camera cannot see. The app searches a photo library with this string, so words a photographer would use beat words a cook would.

image_urls.description: Left to the app. It holds the one photo the cook settled on, or a mise:// photo off their device. Do not emit it: a url you supply overrides the photo search and is usually a 404. Describe the dish in image_query instead. https only — phones block cleartext http.

id.description: 4-char id referenced from step content as {0001}

name.description: Counting noun folded in for whole items, e.g. 'garlic cloves'

density_g_per_ml.description: Grams per millilitre, for ingredients genuinely measurable both ways. Spooned and levelled, not packed: flour 0.53, granulated sugar 0.85, brown sugar 0.93, water 1.0, milk 1.03, oil 0.92, honey 1.42, cocoa 0.51, butter 0.91. Omit for countable items, pinches, and anything only ever measured one way.

timer_seconds.description: Set whenever the step involves waiting: proofing, baking, resting, chilling, simmering
